tagline.text: A monument and mausoleum with 19 steps for the 19 martyrs executed in 1897

location.label: Location
location.text: Poblacion, Kalibo, Aklan, around the corner of Veterans Avenue and M. Acevedo Street

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (dry season November–May recommended, March memorial events)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱50~300 (per person, downtown tricycle and snacks, entrance reported free but not officially confirmed)

children.text: The Aklan Freedom Shrine is a monument and mausoleum in Kalibo honoring the 19 Katipunan martyrs executed by Spanish authorities on March 23, 1897. A statue of their leader, Francisco del Castillo, stands atop 19 steps, and the site was declared a national historical shrine in 2019.

The Aklan Freedom Shrine is a monument and mausoleum in downtown Kalibo. It honors 19 Filipino revolutionaries executed by the Spanish colonial authorities on March 23, 1897, whom Wikipedia calls the "Nineteen Martyrs of Aklan." The more accurate name is the "Nineteen Martyrs of Capiz." At the time, Aklan was not yet a separate province, and all of these men came from towns in Capiz that now belong to Aklan, so "Aklan" is a later label. Eleven were from Kalibo, three from Malinao and five from Lagatik (now New Washington).

The story begins with two migrant workers in Australia. Francisco del Castillo and Candido Iban won a lottery in Australia, returned to Manila in 1894 or 1895 and joined the Katipunan, the secret society aiming for Philippine independence. They donated part of their winnings toward a printing press for Kalayaan, the Katipunan's newspaper, whose first issue appeared in March 1896. Andres Bonifacio directed the two to set up a Katipunan chapter in the Visayas. Del Castillo died in a fight on March 17, 1897, and his death increased revolutionary feeling around Capiz.

The Spanish colonial government promised amnesty to the remaining revolutionaries but instead imprisoned and tortured them. On March 23, 1897, these 19 men were summarily executed on the orders of Spanish colonel Ricardo Monet. The men executed were Roman Aguirre, Tomas Briones, Valeriano Dalida, Domingo de la Cruz, Claro Delgado, Angelo Fernandez, Benito Iban, Candido Iban, Simeon Inocencio, Isidro Jimenez, Catalino Mangat, Lamberto Mangat, Valeriano Masinda, Maximo Mationg, Simplicio Reyes, Canuto Segovia, Gavino Sucgang, Francisco Villorente and Gavino Yunsal. Their remains are said to have been buried elsewhere at first and then exhumed and reinterred in this memorial.

The most striking feature of the shrine is its 19 steps. Each step is dedicated to one martyr, and at the top stands a statue of their leader, Francisco del Castillo. The names of the 19 and of del Castillo are said to be permanently inscribed on the site. On April 25, 2019, the National Historical Commission declared it a national historical shrine, after the Kalibo town council had earlier passed a resolution in 2019 asking for national recognition. One travel guide lists it as free and open daily, 24 hours, but there is no official confirmation, so check locally before you go. Even a short stop makes you reflect on Kalibo's modern history, and it is a good addition to a walking tour of downtown. Knowing the background makes the visit deeper. Aklan was a district of Capiz when civil government was set up in 1901 and became its own province in 1956 when President Ramon Magsaysay signed the law creating it. So the martyrs were people of Capiz in their own time, and people in Kalibo still remember them as forebears who opened the way to freedom in their region. The execution came a year and a half before the Spanish left Kalibo in late December 1898, which hints at how heavy an event it was in the local revolution.
The monument has 19 steps winding upward, and each step is dedicated to one martyr. Climb slowly and think of each name.
At the top of the monument stands a statue of Francisco del Castillo, who led the Katipunan in Capiz (now Aklan). He died in battle on March 17, 1897, so he is not among the 19 executed.
Of those executed, 11 were from Kalibo, 3 from Malinao and 5 from Lagatik. Their names are inscribed at the site, so look for the brothers who share surnames, such as Iban and Mangat.

blocks.title: The lottery and the printing press

children.text: Candido Iban is said to have bought a printing press with lottery winnings from Australia and donated it to the Katipunan. It is the story of an ordinary migrant worker who entered revolutionary history, so it is worth asking a guide about.
On April 25, 2019, the National Historical Commission declared the site a national historical shrine by Resolution No. 8. The Kalibo Historical Society welcomed the decision.
Around March 23, the date of the martyrdom, a memorial event is held in Kalibo every year. The schedule changes each year, so check municipal announcements.

blocks.title: A location suited to a downtown walk

children.text: It is close to the center, where Kalibo Cathedral, Pastrana Park and the museum are gathered, and a short tricycle ride away. It is a good fit for a one-day downtown route.
The 2019 documentary "Daan Patungong Tawaya" ("Road to Paradise") portrays the martyrs as empowered by anting-anting, a kind of amulet. Take a look if you want to see the story on film.
Take a tricycle from your hotel or the airport to the Aklan Freedom Shrine. Early morning is quiet.
Climb the steps of the monument slowly and look at where the names are inscribed.
Pause in front of the statue of del Castillo at the top and take a photo.
Head to the town center and walk Pastrana Park and the cathedral.
View it quietly as a memorial, and follow instructions when an event is being held.
Start with the martyrs' story at the Aklan Freedom Shrine.
See the Aklan history exhibits at Museo it Akean (confirm weekday opening).
Walk Kalibo Cathedral and Pastrana Park.
Have lunch at a restaurant downtown.
Take a tricycle to Bakhawan Eco-Park and walk the boardwalk.
There are direct flights from Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Kalibo International Airport (KLO) taking about
1 hour
. Which airlines fly the route changes, so check when you book.
From the airport you can go to the town center by tricycle or taxi, and one guide says the airport is close enough that it takes about
10~15 minutes
One guide says it takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
from Caticlan, the gateway to Boracay, to Kalibo by bus or van. Before boarding, confirm that you can get off in downtown Kalibo (Poblacion).
Tricycles are the main way to get around Kalibo. The shrine is in Poblacion, near the cathedral and Pastrana Park.
Tell the driver "Aklan Freedom Shrine," and if the location is confusing, search "Aklan Freedom Shrine" in a map app and show it. Agree on the fare first.
The monument is outdoors, so November to May, when it is less rainy and not too hot, is the best time to visit. The midday sun is strong, so morning or late afternoon is easier.

Around March 23, the day of the martyrdom, memorial events are held in Kalibo. In January, when the Ati-Atihan festival is on, downtown is crowded and lodging fills early, but it is actually a good time to look back at the town's history. Event dates change each year, so check the latest announcements.

Hotels cluster in downtown Kalibo (Poblacion), where the shrine is, and along the road to the airport. Choose a place near the airport if you have an early flight or arrive late, and downtown if you want to walk to the shrine, cathedral and museum. During the January Ati-Atihan festival, lodging fills up months ahead and rates rise, so book early. One guide says business hotels run about
a night and simple pensions and guesthouses about
, but prices vary greatly by season. Check the latest reviews and rates on a booking site.

Aklan food makes liberal use of coconut. Binakol, chicken simmered in coconut water, and inubaran, banana stem pith cooked in coconut milk, are the signature dishes. Near the market you can also try grilled skewers and rice cakes (kakanin). No restaurant right next to the shrine was confirmed, so eat at restaurants downtown.
It is a memorial, so dress modestly and do not make loud noise or run on the steps.
The steps can be slippery after rain, so wear comfortable shoes.
The light is soft in the early morning or late afternoon, which is good for photos and avoids the midday heat.
If a guide is available, ask about the 19 men and the lottery and printing press story.
Linking the museum, cathedral and park on foot makes a one-day downtown route with little travel.
It helps to ask a tricycle driver to wait for your return, but agree on the fare first.
Memorial events are held around March 23, so if the dates fit, add them to your plans.
Before you see the monument, skim the museum's exhibit on notable people or the list of names in the overview, and you will enjoy recognizing the inscribed names.
Address spellings differ by source (the corner of Veterans Avenue and M. Acevedo Street, D. Maagma Street and others), so it is quicker to search by name in a map app.

The shrine's entrance fee (reported free), visiting hours (reported 24 hours) and address are either not officially confirmed or differ by source. Ask the municipal tourism office or a local information desk before you visit.
It is a memorial, so avoid noisy behavior and littering.
The steps can be slippery on rainy days, so hold the handrail as you climb.
The date of national recognition differs by source, as April 25 and March 29, 2019. News reports and Wikipedia give April 25.
During the festival, pickpocketing and lost items increase, so leave valuables at your hotel.
It gets dark around the site after sunset, so finish in the afternoon.
Opening hours are not officially confirmed, so if it is closed, see the monument from outside the fence and try again early in the morning.
The Aklan capital
Kalibo
, where the shrine stands, has a cathedral, a market and a mangrove forest.
The
Ati-Atihan Festival
, which fills Kalibo every January, is another face of the town.
Reached via Caticlan,
Boracay
is the best-known beach destination connected to Kalibo.

blocks.title: Museo it Akean and Kalibo Cathedral

children.text: The Aklan museum and St. John the Baptist Cathedral are clustered within walking distance of the town center.
